1.explanation: All of the value-update and increment/decrement logic lives in src/number-picker/index.jsx. That file currently adds step to the current value directly (i.e. 4.02 + 0.01) and doesn’t apply any rounding based on the precision prop, so the native floating-point in Safari shows 4.029999999999999. To fix the bug, index.jsx needs to apply a toFixed or proper rounding helper (using the supplied precision) after each calculation so the displayed and returned values are rounded to two decimal places (e.g. 4.03).
1.bug_scenario: In Safari, using a NumberPicker initialized at 4.02 with step 0.01 (and precision 2) and clicking the “+” button yields 4.029999999999999 instead of the expected 4.03. This is purely a JavaScript floating-point issue that isn’t being corrected/rounded by the component’s increment logic.

2.explanation: The increment and decrement logic for NumberPicker lives in src/number-picker/index.jsx. It currently adds the step to the current value using native JS arithmetic, which in Safari (and all JS engines) exposes floating-point rounding errors. To fix this, the addition should use a precision-aware algorithm (for example multiplying by 10^precision, adding integers, then dividing and toFixed), or leverage a decimal helper, to ensure the displayed value respects the configured precision.
2.bug_scenario: In Safari, when using NumberPicker with a decimal step (e.g. defaultValue=4.02, step=0.01) clicking the "+" button produces the JS floating-point result 4.029999999999999 instead of the expected 4.03. The screenshot shows the field displaying 4.029999999999999 due to raw addition of floats.
